items.title: A Tribe Called Love
items.review: Warra a watch. I think this is one of the most deeply personal experiences I felt with a movie in a longtime. The people I talked to after the film itself, the messaging. The film really did highlights the problems we see plaguing our community, in such a beautiful and comedic way. I remember speaking to a fellow peer of mine that watched the movie as well, and then I asked them, "Hey, what do you think about the movie?" We're casually talking about some of the plot points that were devastating and are actually impacting our lives as well, like gun violence in that aspect. It just shows how prevalent the issue is really. One personal message the director mentioned during Q&A that really stuck with me was the stubborn nature of Somali men and how, in our ways, we tend to harm ourselves or kill ourselves in the process rather than coming together. I'm just super excited for Somali cinema in general. I think seeing this film and the production level, the quality, the acting, I'm just excited for what's coming next, the next wave. I'm ngl, this might be up there for sure, especially for Somali cinema. This is the bar to beat. The animation was superb. Just wowed me; seemed like a personal love letter to Somalia and Toronto. The timeline on this was just nuts: 23 days, 8 hours a day of shooting. Just hearing this is just top-notch stuff, man. I can't wait to see all the other stuff from Mawimbi and Mohammed himself, Phenomenal Film. If you’re an Aspiring SOMALI CINEPHILE PICKUP THE CAMERA and shoot something, LIKE MOHAMED said. 🩵🇸🇴

items.title: Backrooms
items.review: "It's every place that ever was." WE NEED MORE GEN-Z directors genuinely!! the camera work and the score and 1-1 adaption phenomenal!!! 1. I really love the analog horror, the cinematography, and also the color palette. No one truly understands how beautiful the camerawork in this movie was it felt alive and as viewer it felt so dreadful. I felt a part of the sequence literally the insect was one of those cool shots that gave me that joy. The next cool shot I would say was when it pans over and zooms into the liminal spaces, and you feel the existential dread. One thing that's really cool about this film that I said earlier is that the place has so much familiarity, and the score and the SFX are very, very close to home. When I mean that, it's like if you worked in a shitty office ever in your life, you know that experience where the light is flickering or even the humming of lights. It's one of those things that are a nuisance, but it's turned into horror element, which is so amazing. These Gen Z directors, even seeing the series turn into a movie, SPECTACULAR GIVE ME 14 of them . Love it. I would have given it a five if I didn't miss the five-minute sequence in the beginning, but I must rewatch this to give my full honest confident take and also understand most of motifs I’ve missed or too afraid to notice 😭😭. Honestly, I think this is Jaws moment for our generation. I'm certain people are going to be more afraid of liminal spaces, long hallways, or anything yellowstained 😭😭. just wow, just what a film, what a film. I can't wait to rewatch it again, hopefully. 🫣

items.title: Che: Part One
items.review: Sidenote: this review is super super shallow and superficial. I want to see part two and condense everything into one review, but I just wanted to still speak on Benicio's character and portraying Che so well. This was really amazing, Highkey I think this might be one of those biopics that is up there for me depending on pt2. I've loved Benicio del Toro's work in OBAA and to see him having his mc moment in CHE. It's really impressive to see him portray and emulate Che, one of the most enigmatic historical icons, in such a profound way. I paused the movie during the UN delegation scene and rewatched the real events on YouTube that Che gave. It wasn't exactly one-to-one, but the way Benicio steps into the character's shoes and emulates him shows the range he has. I remember watching OBAA; I didn't know the context of his character, and now, seeing his other work in CHE Part 1, you truly see why he was amazing. Shoutout to PTA for casting him in OBAA. Ironically, this film centers around CHE, and I've seen some reviews critiquing how the cinematography and atmosphere shift from Part 1 to Part 2. I'm really excited to see Part 2, but what a film, what a quote. "Patria o Muerte" , SHIVERS warra watch.

items.title: The Drama
items.review: Update: didn't feel rating this same as Obsession 4 -> 4.5 I need a walk after watching this (ᵕ–﹏–)🌡️ Loved the really cool intricate details that I related with Emma character, I'm in deaf in my right ear also and get those random moments where people think I'm ignoring them, or I have trouble hearing them 😭😭 I initially came in blind, I was expecting a lot but got more ngl. I love how the movie danced around the idea of intimacy how it's really really personal *and unique to each couple despite how unusual it seemed & shouldn't be shared with friends or especially with acquaintances.(HOT_TAKE: Rachel is walking red flag for not keeping her vow with her mans) But it seemed Charlie really and dearly loved Emma and so did Emma, Even that speech he worked on in the beginning it was really beautiful was so real and vulnerable, it's quite sad a granular conflict between his friends and fiancée shaped how he saw her, but to me it’s also quite ironic, but it's funny this conflict was Charlie's worst thing he has ever done, and shockingly it was to Emma. Long story short Emma's ability to recognized that and letting him have do-over was beautiful (Charlie is still a bot IMO) I think this is Roberts's & Zendaya's best work, I went in blind and still felt shocked how much chemistry they had. The second-hand embrassement, the small disagreements, the puns good stuff!! Wish I have seen this in theaters
